newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two dead, others lost in German building collapse.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, others lost in German building collapse.

text.p: German rescue workers recovered the bodies of two woman and said at least five people might still be buried under a four-storey house which collapsed early on Thursday after a suspected gas explosion.
Rescuers earlier managed to pull a 60-year-old woman and a 31-year-old Polish man, both seriously injured, from the rubble of the house after they heard knocking sounds.
Senior investigator Hubert Steiger said the search team had not given up hope that they could find people alive, but he added: "We must assume that we could find more dead."

Police said they could not be sure exactly how many people they were missing. Some 15 people were registered as living in the building. Six or seven of them were believed to be away on holiday but others could have been visiting the apartments.
Residents said the house collapsed at 0100 GMT and they reported hearing a number of explosions. Dozens of windows in the surrounding area were shattered.
Police evacuated surrounding buildings because they suspected a gas leak under the house caused the explosion.
Prosecutor Hans-Rainer Kleinert said he had ruled out the possibility of a racist attack because Germans lived alongside Poles, Portugese and Japanese in the apartment block.
